Ben / team — I reviewed the proposed schedule. A few accounting constraints from Redwood's side:
- Under ASC 606 (and most similar frameworks), revenue is recognized over time as services are provided. For prepaid committed capacity, we typically recognize ratably over the service period unless there are distinct performance obligations that justify another pattern.
- Invoicing split is acceptable so long as the contract and our AR reflect the single economic transaction. We'll need the contract to state the payment schedule and the invoiced amounts and to reference the single commitment.
- Discounts: to avoid recognition complexity, we prefer applying the commercial discount at the time of invoicing (i.e., invoice reflects the discounted amounts). If you need a true-up (e.g., discount based on achieved usage), we require a clearly defined true-up mechanism and timing to account for subsequent adjustments.

Suggested invoice allocation for a 3-year commitment (example only):
- Year 1 (FY26): 45% invoice issued at signing (covers Oct year timing constraints noted below)
- Year 2 (FY27): 35% invoice at start of FY27
- Year 3 (FY28): 20% final invoice

Please note: Acme's fiscal year start will affect when we book AR vs recognize income. If Acme prefers invoices aligned to their FY (Oct 1), we can adapt the issue dates but need to document the single transaction in the contract.

Attachment: acct-treatment-notes.pdf (short memo on recognition approach and sample journal entries)
